current.text: Dusty May is the new Dallas head coach. He says Flagg will play positions one through four this season, including some guard.
With Kyrie Irving back and a new coach, his role may change. If he plays the four next to other power forwards, his fantasy situation gets worse.
Dallas is short on ball handlers. Kyrie Irving, rookie Sergio de Larrea and Marcus Sasser are the only real guards, and Kyrie is 36 and coming off injury.

Flagg is the first option on offense and Kyrie Irving is second. Kyrie may cut into his assists a little, but he should take shots mostly from other players. With so few ball handlers, Flagg keeps the ball in his hands.
Dallas has too many power forwards, so Flagg is unlikely to get chances for big block numbers.

Experts expect his scoring and efficiency to rise, with assists going from 4.5 to over 5 and a chance of more steals or blocks. Josh expects him to start the season close to the level he ended last season at. The open question is whether his shooting improves.
Dusty May says he will push Flagg to take more threes.

In category leagues, experts are happy to take him at the end of round one or the start of round two. Josh calls him an absolute bargain at his ADP and would take him as high as pick 9. Getting him in round two is called fantastic.
Several experts see him as a top 10 to top 12 player. They call his ESPN ADP, around 17 to 24, free value.
In auctions, Josh would pay about 40 USD. He called 42 USD in a mock high, and an average auction price of 60 USD is called way too high.
Dallas has a 4-4-4 schedule in the fantasy playoffs, probably the best in the league. It also has a league-high 16 back-to-backs and a two-game week in the matchup starting March 1.
Dallas has no reason to tank because its pick is owed, so a late-season shutdown is unlikely. Projections range from a bad team to a 41-win play-in team.

durable.text: Won Rookie of the Year. Dallas gave him heavy usage down the stretch, and he finished 14th in category leagues over the final two months.
He is a 6'11 forward who handles the ball, scores and distributes on high usage, and protects the rim from the weak side.
The experts call him a budding superstar.
Three-point shooting is a weakness. He shot about 29% from three as a rookie, and he did less rim protecting than hoped.
A perimeter role tends to cost him rebounds and blocks. Playing the four does not hurt his assists.
He contributes across categories: points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and FT%. Rebounds and blocks are high for a G/F. Turnovers are his weak category.
Experts rate him a little higher in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: Flagg costs a late first-round price. The market lists him at 50.6 USD on Yahoo and 41.4 USD on ESPN, and Josh caps him at about 40 USD. Our league got him for 25 USD as a rookie, but that price will not repeat. He gives value in almost every category, with turnovers as the only weak spot, so he fits most builds and especially punt TO. Dallas also has a 4-4-4 playoff schedule. Early in the season, check whether Dusty May uses him at guard or at the four, whether his three-point shooting improves from about 29%, and whether the crowded frontcourt cuts his blocks.
